objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a breast mass.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Hello, doctor. I noticed a mass in my right breast about three weeks ago, and it’s been rapidly getting bigger. I haven’t had any pain, and I haven’t noticed any changes in the skin or nipple.”
“Yes, doctor—I'm 45 years old. The mass started about three weeks ago on my right breast and has been enlarging quickly, without pain or skin/nipple changes.”
Does the mass feel hard or soft, and does it move freely under the skin or feel fixed in place?
“It feels hard, and it doesn’t seem to move much under the skin—it feels fairly fixed in place.”
Have you noticed any lumps or swelling in your right armpit or near your collarbone?
“No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any lumps or swelling in my right armpit or near my collarbone.”
Do you have a personal or family history of breast or ovarian cancer, or any known genetic mutations like BRCA?
“No, doctor—there’s no personal history of breast or ovarian cancer, and no family history either, and I don’t know of any genetic mutations like BRCA in my family.”
Have you had any recent trauma, injury, or surgery to your right breast or chest area?
“Doctor, no—I haven’t had any recent trauma, injury, or surgery to my right breast or chest area.”
Have you noticed any nipple discharge from the right breast, and if so, what is its color or consistency?
“No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any nipple discharge from my right breast.”
Are you currently pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking any hormonal medications (such as oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy)?
“No, doctor—I’m not pregnant or breastfeeding, and I’m not taking any hormonal medications like birth control pills or hormone replacement therapy.”
Have you experienced any unexplained weight loss, fever, night sweats, or unusual fatigue recently?
“No, doctor—I haven’t had any unexplained weight loss, fever, night sweats, or unusual fatigue recently.”
